Names and terms Amber should spell right

Whisper and the servers of OpenAI and Groq get the first few dozen as a hint; the cleanup gets all of them and keeps their spelling. Parakeet and Android\'s speech recognition cannot take them. The list stays on this phone; a server gets it only with a dictation.
None yet. Several at once: separate them with commas.
%1$d of %2$d - the list is full. Tap a word to remove it.

All of it works by rules, without a language model, so nothing is made up. The commas go before \"dass\", \"weil\", \"wenn\" or \"um ... zu\", where recognition often leaves them out - they never change a word. Spoken punctuation knows comma, period or full stop, question mark, exclamation mark, colon, new line and new paragraph - in German Komma, Punkt, Fragezeichen, Ausrufezeichen, Doppelpunkt, neue Zeile and neuer Absatz -, each in a dictation of its language. Where the word belongs to the sentence (\"a comma is missing\", \"Punkt zwölf\") it stays a word. \"Scratch that\" or \"streich das\" at the very end of a dictation takes back the sentence before it.
Say \"comma\", \"period\", \"new line\" - in German \"Komma\", \"Punkt\", \"neue Zeile\". \"Scratch that\" or \"streich das\" at the end takes back the sentence before it
Longer dictations are cut at pauses and recognized while you keep talking, so stopping only waits for the last part.

Optional. Keeps Android from cutting off the microphone.

Android may cut off the microphone of an app in the background. The microphone service keeps it ready while you are in other apps, its silent notification says so, and unrestricted battery stops some manufacturers from killing the service.
